qt: to the Commission Emmanouil Fragkos (ECR) Subject:

Farming in the Philippi marshes is heavily dependent on electricity-powered borehole drilling, pumping stations and irrigation, drying and storage systems. The increase in electricity costs places a disproportionate burden on producers of maize, sunflower and other energy-intensive crops, limiting agricultural income and the region’s competitiveness. The production of energy for self-consumption, the collective production of energy by cooperatives and local land reclamation organisations, as well as energy upgrades in agricultural facilities could permanently reduce production costs. However, high upfront costs, the lack of available hosting capacity, connection delays and procedural complexity put off many small and medium-sized producers from harnessing these solutions. The CAP Strategic Plans can fund productive investments and renewable energy sources and EU State aid rules allow support for investment in farms, subject to conditions. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Which CAP and cohesion policy instruments can fund collective self-production and energy storage projects for farmers, cooperatives and land reclamation organisations in the Philippi marshes?
Can priority grid connections and increased aid intensity be envisaged for farmer-led energy communities in agricultural areas with high productivity?
Does it intend to encourage a specific intervention in the Greek CAP Strategic Plan to reduce the energy costs of primary production?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.10.2026) Under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP)1 Member States may, based on their needs assessment and strategies, provide support for investments in energy production and storage through their CAP Strategic Plans (CSP). The Greek CSP provides for a specific intervention for investment in the energy domain, prioritising the use of renewable energy resources2. This includes financial support for investments in renewable energy production in agriculture. Moreover, under the Horizon Europe work programmes3 and in synergy with the Innovation Fund under the Emission Trading Scheme, Greek entities in the agricultural domain may participate in research and innovation initiatives relating to energy generation in agriculture. State aid rules provide possibilities of investment aid to farmers for energy production to cover own needs or even beyond the self-consumption level. Cohesion policy may support energy communities under the relevant specific objective relating to the promotion of renewable energy sources. EU’s electricity market legislation does not provide automatic priority grid connection for specific end uses. However, if necessary, national regulatory authorities may establish a grid connection prioritisation framework based on objective, transparent and non-discriminatory criteria, as set out in the Commission’s Guidance on efficient and timely grid connections4 and proposed in the proposal for a Regulation as regards future proofing electricity bills in the Union5. Where network capacity is limited or unavailable, Article 6a of Directive (EU) 2019/9446 provides for frameworks allowing flexible connection agreements, including for energy storage. The Greek CSP contains interventions for farm modernisation, improving irrigation efficiency, agricultural roadworks and others, all of which contribute to reduce the energy costs of primary production.
